name: Medicare Part B (J6, National Government Services)

panel.note: Enroll or opt out; there is no panel closure. Medicare Advantage plans credential separately.

source.quote: If I don't enroll, do I need to opt-out to continue to see Medicare beneficiaries?

LCSW.note: Clinical social workers are a Medicare benefit category (42 CFR 410.73): master's or doctorate in social work plus 2 years of supervised clinical work, and your Illinois LCSW. Enroll as Licensed Clinical Social Worker (Medicare specialty 80). You sign the same agreement to consult with the patient's doctor as psychologists do.

source.quote: After obtaining the degree, has performed at least 2 years of supervised clinical social work

LCPC.note: Your Illinois LCPC enrolls as a Mental Health Counselor (42 CFR 410.54), covered since 2024-01-01. Needs 2 years or 3,000 hours of post-master's supervised counseling experience (usually met by the LCPC itself) and the full license. The supervised LPC level is not the independent path. Counselor taxonomy for Medicare: 101YM0800X.

source.quote: Per 42 CFR § 410.54(a)(3), an MHC must be licensed or certified as an MHC, clinical professional counselor, professional counselor

LMFT.note: Marriage and family therapists are covered since 2024-01-01 (42 CFR 410.53). Needs 2 years or 3,000 hours of post-master's supervised experience in marriage and family therapy and your full Illinois LMFT. Enroll as Marriage and Family Therapist (NUCC 106H00000X).

source.quote: at least 2 years or 3,000 hours of post master's degree clinical supervised experience in marriage and family therapy

Psychologist.note: Clinical psychologists are a Medicare benefit category (42 CFR 410.71): a doctorate in psychology and a license at the independent practice level. Enroll as Clinical Psychologist (Medicare specialty 68). Signing the enrollment form is your agreement to the doctor-consultation rules.

source.quote: at the independent practice level of psychology to furnish diagnostic, assessment, preventive, and therapeutic services directly to individuals

requirements.npi: type1 (type2 too if a PLLC bills as a group)
requirements.ein: SSN or EIN for a sole practitioner; EIN required for a PLLC group
requirements.malpractice: No set Medicare minimum found; carry your own coverage
other: Active full Illinois license
CMS-855I (individual) via PECOS or paper; PLLC group also files CMS-855B and each clinician reassigns benefits
I&A (Identity and Access) account needed for PECOS
MFT/MHC: proof of the 2-year/3,000-hour experience may be requested from the licensing board on letterhead
MFTs and MHCs are limited screening risk
Opt-out alternative: file affidavit with the MAC and use private contracts; renews every 2 years

source.quote: MFTs and MHCs are limited risk.

timeline.text: About 15 days for a clean web application, 30 days for a clean paper one (MAC processing); allow more if development letters are needed

source.quote: all clean web applications will be processed within 15 calendar days following receipt, and all clean paper applications will be processed within 30 calendar days

fees.text: No application fee for MFTs and MHCs; the same is generally true for individual practitioners (psychologists, CSWs not confirmed this run)

source.quote: MFTs and MHCs are not required to pay an application fee.

recredential.text: Revalidate about every 5 years; MAC sends notice 3-4 months before due date

source.quote: In general, providers and suppliers revalidate every five years

steps.title: Confirm your NPI and PECOS login
steps.how: Make sure your individual NPI is active and uses the right taxonomy code: LCSW 1041C0700X, LCPC 101YM0800X (Medicare counselor code), LMFT 106H00000X, psychologist 103TC0700X. Then create or sign in to your Identity and Access (I&A) account, which lets you use PECOS.

source.quote: MFTs and MHCs can enroll electronically using the Provider Enrollment, Chain, and Ownership System (PECOS) or the paper CMS-855I enrollment application.

steps.title: Gather your enrollment details
steps.how: Have ready your Illinois license number, degree and school, practice address, tax ID and banking details for payment.

source.quote: MFTs and MHCs can enroll electronically using the Provider Enrollment, Chain, and Ownership System (PECOS) or the paper CMS-855I enrollment application.

how_by_license.LCSW: Have ready your Illinois LCSW number, your MSW or doctorate and school, practice address, tax ID and banking details for payment.
how_by_license.Psychologist: Have ready your Illinois clinical psychologist license number, your doctorate in psychology and school, practice address, tax ID and banking details for payment.
how_by_license.LMFT: Have ready your Illinois LMFT number, degree and school, practice address, tax ID and banking details. Also line up proof of your 2 years or 3,000 hours of supervised experience (next step).
how_by_license.LCPC: Have ready your Illinois LCPC number, degree and school, practice address, tax ID and banking details. Also line up proof of your 2 years or 3,000 hours of supervised counseling experience (next step).

steps.title: Show your 2 years of supervised experience
steps.how: If Illinois already required that experience for your license, do nothing: the Medicare contractor checks it. If not, send a signed letter on letterhead (not email) from a past employer or supervisor, or from your licensing body, confirming 2 years or 3,000 hours.

source.quote: If the clinical experience is not part of obtaining a license, the practitioner will need to submit documentation with their application

steps.title: Submit your Medicare enrollment
steps.how: Log in to PECOS and answer the questions; it builds the CMS-855I for you. Only you may sign it. If you have a PLLC billing as a group, the group also files a CMS-855B and you reassign your benefits to it.

source.quote: MFTs and MHCs can enroll electronically using the Provider Enrollment, Chain, and Ownership System (PECOS) or the paper CMS-855I enrollment application.

how_by_license.Psychologist: Log in to PECOS and answer the questions; it builds the CMS-855I for you. Choose the specialty Clinical Psychologist. Only you may sign it, and your signature is your agreement to the doctor-consultation rules. With a PLLC billing as a group, the group also files a CMS-855B and you reassign your benefits to it.
how_by_license.LCSW: Log in to PECOS and answer the questions; it builds the CMS-855I for you. Choose the specialty Clinical Social Worker. Only you may sign it. With a PLLC billing as a group, the group also files a CMS-855B and you reassign your benefits to it.
how_by_license.LMFT: Log in to PECOS and answer the questions; it builds the CMS-855I for you. Choose the specialty Marriage and Family Therapist. If you use the paper form instead, pick Undefined Non-Physician Practitioner in section 2H and write MFT. Only you may sign it. A PLLC billing as a group also files a CMS-855B.
how_by_license.LCPC: Log in to PECOS and answer the questions; it builds the CMS-855I for you. Choose the specialty Mental Health Counselor (you enroll as MHC, not LCPC). On the paper form, pick Undefined Non-Physician Practitioner in section 2H and write MHC. Only you may sign it. A PLLC billing as a group also files a CMS-855B.

steps.title: Answer any request from the MAC
steps.how: National Government Services (the Illinois Medicare contractor) may email or mail you for missing items. You have 30 days to answer.

source.quote: The provider will have 30 calendar days to respond.

steps.title: Sign and return the contract
steps.how: When the payer sends the participation agreement, read it, sign it and return it the way they say. Keep a copy.

source.quote: Not applicable: Medicare has no contract; you receive an approval letter and a PTAN instead

steps.title: Check the fee schedule
steps.how: Look up the rates for the codes you bill (for example 90791, 90834, 90837) and make sure they work for your practice before you sign.

source.quote: Not applicable: Medicare has no contract; you receive an approval letter and a PTAN instead

steps.title: Note your effective date
steps.how: Your Medicare billing start is the day you filed an application that was later approved (or the day you began at a new location, if later). Write it down from your approval letter.

source.quote: The date of filing of a Medicare enrollment application that was subsequently approved by a Medicare contractor

steps.title: Ask about billing back to the effective date
steps.how: Medicare lets you bill for visits up to 30 days before your effective date if you could not enroll first and met every requirement. Ask your contractor how to send those claims.

source.quote: Thirty days prior to their effective date if circumstances precluded enrollment in advance of providing services to Medicare

notes: Illinois Part B MAC is J6, National Government Services (verified on cms.gov). The old WPS assumption is outdated: WPS handed Part B to NGS on 2021-01-01.
Contracting steps for Medicare are really: accept assignment or not (participating vs non-participating), review the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule, note effective date. No separate contract.
Medicare pays MFT/MHC at 75% of the clinical psychologist rate (secondary sources, unverified).
CMS-855R reassignment is possibly folded into 855I/PECOS (commercial source only); confirm.
NGS site now sits under a Wellpoint Federal address; enrollment details there were not readable this run.

Retroactive billing: up to 30 days before the effective date if circumstances precluded enrolling first (42 CFR 424.521(a)(1)(i), read on law.cornell.edu). Effective date is the filing date of an application later approved (424.520(d)).
Paper CMS-855I has no MFT/MHC line: pick Undefined Non-Physician Practitioner in section 2H and write MFT or MHC (CMS MFT/MHC FAQ, read). PECOS lists the specialties.

Illinois LCPC qualifies as MHC (CMS FAQ lists clinical professional counselor); it must meet the 2 years/3,000 hours rule. CMS taxonomy: MFT 106H00000X, MHC 101YM0800X (FAQ, read). Specialty codes: psychologist 68, licensed clinical social worker 80 (CMS crosswalk, read); MFT/MHC codes not found on a CMS page.

name: TRICARE West Region (TriWest Healthcare Alliance)

panel.note: TriWest takes interest forms; behavioral health openings not published. Being TRICARE-authorized lets you bill out of network without joining.

source.quote: TriWest is accepting interest forms from providers who wish to join the TriWest network.

LCSW.note: Certified clinical social worker (32 CFR 199.6(c)(3)(iii)(F)): MSW from a CSWE-accredited school, 2 years or 3,000 hours post-master's supervised clinical practice, and your Illinois LCSW. No physician referral needed.

source.quote: A clinical social worker may provide covered services independent of physician referral and supervision

LCPC.note: Must meet TRICARE's counselor standard (TCMHC): independent mental health counseling license, CACREP-accredited master's, NCMHCE (an NCE was accepted before 2017), and 2 years with 3,000 supervised hours and 100 hours face-to-face supervision. Counselors who fall short are only 'supervised' counselors, who need a physician referral and oversight and are excluded by TriWest. Check your degree and exam.

source.quote: must be licensed for independent practice in mental health counseling by the jurisdiction where practicing

LMFT.note: Certified marriage and family therapist (32 CFR 199.6(c)(3)(iv)(A)): master's degree, supervised training hours (for example 200 supervision hours and 1,000 clinical hours), your Illinois LMFT, and a participation agreement accepting TRICARE's allowed charge as payment in full.

source.quote: Is licensed or certified to practice as a marriage and family therapist by the jurisdiction where practicing

Psychologist.note: Clinical psychologist (32 CFR 199.6(c)(3)(iii)(A)): doctorate in psychology from a regionally accredited school, 2 years supervised experience (1 post-doctoral) or listing in the National Register, plus your independent Illinois license. No physician referral needed.

source.quote: a clinical psychologist is an individual who is licensed or certified by the state for the independent practice of psychology

other: TriWest uses Aperture Credentialing; CAQH or TriWest application form FS42045 (search summary)

steps.title: Check you meet TRICARE's counselor standards
steps.how: TRICARE has its own bar for counselors. You need: your independent LCPC; a master's from a CACREP-accredited counseling program; a passing NCMHCE score (an NCE score counted before 2017); and 2 years of post-master's work with 3,000 supervised hours and 100 hours of face-to-face supervision. If any piece is missing, TRICARE treats you as a 'supervised' counselor, who needs physician referral and oversight and cannot join the TriWest network. Ask TriWest to confirm before you apply.
